newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Activists block Dutch Unilever plant over gene soya.
newsitem.headline: Activists block Dutch Unilever plant over gene soya.

text.p: Environmental group Milieudefensie, an affiliate of Friends of the Earth, on Thursday blockaded a Dutch Unilever plant as part of its protests over genetically-engineered soybeans.
"We are demanding the labelling of products containing gene-soya," Milieudefensie spokesman Victor van den Belt said.

He told Reuters some 50 activists were blocking the delivery entrance to the Unimills plant in Zwijndrecht, near Rotterdam, which processes edible oils including soyoil for use in Unilever products such as margerine.
"We have formed a blockade and have erected a banner over the gates, which says 'Gene-soya must be labelled'," he said.

A Unilever spokesman in Rotterdam confirmed the protest but said there were less than 50 activists outside the gates. He said the plant management had spoken to them and promised to pass on their concerns to Unilever top management.
But he added Unilever's stance on the issue had not changed.
"The company doesn't see any reason not to use this soya in its products, it's perfectly safe," he said. "Of course, the public has to be well informed but that is happening."
Milieudefensie said it expected to end the action at around 1600 GMT. There were no plans to return on Friday.

Greenpeace has led a campaign across Europe against the imports of the genetically-engineered beans, which have been developed by U.S. chemicals giant Monsanto to be resistant to its weedkiller Round Up.

The environmental group has also targetted what it says are illegal imports of genetically-modified maize, made by Swiss company Ciba Giegy CIGZsn.Z. The European Commission is due to decide on December 18 whether to allow imports of the maize.
Greenpeace activists in Germany on Thursday disrupted the loading of U.S. feed maize, believed to contain genetically-manipulated strains, onto trains bound for the Czech republic.
Others also blocked a barge on the Rhine river, claiming it was illegally taking gene-modified soybeans to Switzerland.
